tasks.short: Observe the patient's vital signs during the operation and judge their condition.

steps.what: Observe patients and vital signs throughout the operation
Commit the physical condition sentence on the patient record

tasks.design: The surgical technologist still stands in the theatre and watches the patient and the patient monitor ({OTHER}) for the whole case. A change is said to the circulating nurse in the room, as part of that watch. The condition sentence is then committed on the patient record ({OTHER}), with the heart rate, pressure and saturation already confirmed from the monitor; the technologist checks those three values against the patient before the note is committed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Judging a draped patient is the work, and a wrong call can harm them. Retyping the monitor numbers into a side note did not make that judgement any safer.
tasks.enabler_now: The patient monitor already keeps heart rate, blood pressure and oxygen saturation with a time. A note field on the patient record can hold the condition sentence beside the readings the technologist has just confirmed. No model judges the patient.
tasks.still_hard: A bad cuff, a loose lead or a cold hand can make the monitor disagree with the patient. Only the person in the room can see that. Who may write on the surgical record depends on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that the patient is paler, or that a pressure fall is the cuff and not a bleed, and saying so while the case is still open.
tasks.altitude: The technologist still watches every case and still decides when a change needs the team. The week changes only in the note: three numbers are not retyped when the confirmed readings are attached. They do not gain the right to interpret signs for the anaesthetist.

reach.task: Set the vital-sign limits for this patient and judge a change during the operation
reach.learn: Which changes they want called out in the room, so the condition sentence matches that limit

reach.task: Chart vital values on the intraoperative record during the case
reach.learn: Which of those values the chart already stores, so the note adds the condition the technologist saw

evidence.claim: A theatre patient monitor keeps numeric vital signs with a time, and a person in the room still has to judge whether those numbers match the patient.
Health data are a special category, so a condition note on the patient record is health data.
The medical file is kept for 20 years, and this condition note is part of that file.

assumptions: Time split follows the means. Documents 4.5 become 5 and in-person work stays 95. Screens 0.3, spreadsheets 0.1 and mail 0.1 are omitted: each is under 1, and this design does not use them.

The patient monitor produces heart rate, systolic pressure, diastolic pressure, oxygen saturation and the time. The technologist confirms those readings in the watch. If the link to the patient record is down, they type the three values, and that time stays inside the note step.
About two fifths of today's note is retyping those values. The rest is the condition sentence and the check that the cuff and the lead match the patient. That is why the note step remains at 60.
Saying a change to the circulating nurse is live talk with a colleague, inside the watch. It is not a message and not a record, so it has no step of its own and no gate.
The design does not score how fast the technologist responds, and it does not use the readings to judge them. Focal upkeep is zero. A clinical engineer keeps the field names mapped.
Nothing in this design interprets the signs. The person writes the condition sentence. The committed note is the final version; no later step edits it.
unknowns: Whether this theatre's monitor feed already lands on the surgical record.
Whether the circulating nurse must countersign the note under this hospital's rules.
Which national consultation applies before a new field is added to the surgical record.
research_questions: Which three values does this theatre's monitor keep with a reliable time?
Does the circulating nurse already chart the same numbers, so the technologist's note would repeat them?

already_counted.description: Writing the condition sentence and checking the three confirmed readings before the note is committed.

incremental.description: A clinical engineer keeps the monitor field names mapped on the patient record.

approvals.approved_version: condition note committed on the patient record

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net is 2: the watch stays at 100, the note is 5 points with 60 remaining, and focal upkeep is zero. High is 1, when the confirmed readings attach and only the condition sentence is typed. Low is 0, when the link is down and the technologist types heart rate, pressure and saturation by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technologist still stands in every case and still judges the patient's condition. The only change in the week is the note: three numbers come from the confirmed monitor readings when the link is up. There is no new right to interpret signs for the anaesthetist.
reach: Anesthesiologists: learn the limits set for this patient so a call-out matches the change they want during the case.
Registered Nurses: learn which vital values the intraoperative chart already holds so the note adds only the condition seen.
skills_to_grow: Match a monitor number to the patient, including a bad cuff or a loose lead.
Say a short condition sentence to the circulating nurse while the case is open.
Check the three attached readings against the patient before the note is committed.
Keep the difference between watching a sign and interpreting it for anaesthesia.
role.ambitious_version: The condition sentence is on the patient record before the patient leaves the theatre, with the confirmed readings beside it, after the technologist has already said the change in the room.
